1. Error cases: invalid metadata → {"error":"invalid"}; invalid capture → {"error":"capture"}; metadata error takes precedence.
2. Revision reconciliation: conflicts, tombstones, resurrection.
3. Lease census: alias, conflict, inactive, unresolved.
4. App census: eligibility, causality (witness <= event), max attempt, signature agreement, protocol errors.
5. zstd captures.
6. Planning: quotas, min cost.
7. Certificate semantics.

Let me write a test script that builds campaigns and checks the outputs.

But first, let me re-read the PROTOCOL to double check a few subtle points I may have glossed over.

Re-reading key paragraphs:

"### Invocation and errors
Each invocation is `python3 -I -B /workspace/submission/campaign.py`, with one UTF-8 JSON object on stdin (at most 64 MiB) and one UTF-8 JSON object on stdout.
Whitespace around JSON is allowed; a BOM, duplicate object keys, nonfinite numbers and trailing records are invalid. Integer fields require JSON integers, never booleans or floating-point values. Object key order and JSON whitespace do not matter. Every specified object has exactly its listed keys."

✓ handled.

"Invalid root metadata/JSON produces exactly {"error":"invalid"}. With valid metadata, invalid capture transport/encoding/header or exceeded capture bounds produces exactly {"error":"capture"}. A bad logical data record is instead omitted and its index reported; it never invalidates the envelope. Open device responses with bad wire framing remain valid records with unknown service state. When both metadata and captures are bad, the metadata error takes precedence. Exit zero after a complete result; diagnostics belong on stderr." ✓

"### Metadata and target manifest ... Queries are 1–4 distinct times; process/report them in increasing order." ✓

"A lease is {id,prefix,start,end,subnets,low_count}. There are at most 2048.
The prefix is a strict /56 or /64 network in the documentation range, with no host bits, zone ID or whitespace. start<end; its interval is [start,end).
subnets has 1–16 distinct integers: 0–255 for /56, or only 0 for /64.
low_count is 1–32. Each subnet selects the /64 whose network integer is lease_network + (subnet << 64). For each selected /64, plan one canary and low IIDs1 through low_count. Across leases this is at most 65536 targets, including canaries and repeats in overlapping leases." ✓

"The canary IID is the first eight SHA256 digest bytes, interpreted big endian, ORed with 2^63. Hash UTF-8 seed + "\n" + lease_id + "\n" + canonical_/64 with no trailing newline; canonical_/64 is the lowercase compressed network with /64." ✓

"The target is the /64 network plus its IID. Probe IDs are subnet/c and subnet/iN using ordinary decimal subnet and IID numbers without leading zeros. manifest contains {lease,probe,target} in lexical lease-ID order, then numeric subnet order, then canary followed by increasing low IID." ✓

"### Capture transport and typed records ... 0–16 captures ... There are at most 1024 chunks total and 32 MiB decoded bytes total. Empty chunks are allowed." ✓

"Each capture independently yields a UTF-8 CSV stream; chunks may split any code point, compressed frame or CSV record." ✓

"Zstandard captures contain complete, dictionary-free frames with window at most 128 MiB; concatenated and skippable frames are allowed. The unused frame-header bit is ignored; its reserved bit must be zero. Truncation, checksum or frame errors invalidate the capture. Total decompressed bytes (plain CSV also counts) are at most 128 MiB." ✓

"CSV uses the CPython 3.11 csv.reader default Excel dialect with strict=True and newline='': comma delimiter, double-quote quoting and doubled quotes, no escape character, CRLF/LF record endings. Quoted fields can contain newlines. The first logical record of every capture is exactly: ..." ✓

"At most 200000 logical data records occur across captures. Each field is at most 131072 UTF-8 bytes. A blank logical data record counts and is malformed." ✓

"For record failures report [capture_index,logical_data_ordinal], both zero based; the header is excluded. Preserve capture/record order in rejected." ✓

"Wrong field count, bad types/references/addresses, and violations below are record failures." ✓

"Every record has 14 string fields. type is icmp or app; id is an ID; revision is 0–10^9; published is a time; op is put or delete. CSV integers consist of 1–16 ASCII decimal digits; leading zeros are allowed." ✓

"A delete has the first five fields above and all remaining fields empty. A put references a known lease; event is a time in that lease interval and event<=published. Its target is a documentation address." ✓

"An ICMP put has a probe from that lease's manifest and the numerically equal planned target. result is echo, error or timeout. A timeout has an empty responder; other results require a documentation responder. service, attempt and payload are empty. An error from the target is not a positive self echo." ✓

"An application put has empty probe and responder, a known service and an attempt integer 0–10^6. result is open, closed or timeout. payload is base64 with decoded size at most 65536 bytes. Closed/timeouts require an empty payload; TCP requires an empty payload for all results. Other open payloads may be wire-malformed and still constitute valid application rows. No requirement makes an app target a planned address or requires discovery to precede the row; causality is assessed after reconciliation." ✓

"### Publication, revisions and lease census
The identity of a record is (type,id), global across captures. At query q only valid rows with published<=q exist. The highest visible revision wins; lower revisions never repair a conflicting higher revision. At that revision, collapse identical semantic contents, ignoring publication time and spelling differences in addresses, decimal integers and base64. Content includes op and every typed put field; all deletes have identical content. Multiple distinct contents mean one conflicted identity and contribute no live record. A unique delete is a tombstone; a later higher put can resurrect it. Identical copies count once.
ledger reports {live,deleted,conflict} identity counts, including live records whose lease is inactive at q. Invalid rows never enter this ledger." ✓

"For each active lease, derive raw internal I and external E from its live ICMP: positive self echoes of low targets add the responder to I; any non-timeout low probe answered by a different address adds that responder to E. A self error adds neither. A positive self echo of any canary marks the whole lease aliased; other canary responses add neither I nor E. The earliest live ICMP event that supports each (role,address) is that role's causal witness. Duplicate distinct identities can support the same address; withdrawal can remove its last witness." ✓

"Raw conflicts is I intersect E. State priority is: inactive outside the lease interval; otherwise alias if marked; otherwise conflict for nonempty conflicts; otherwise usable. Quarantined leases (alias/conflict) expose empty clean I/E and no witnesses. Inactive leases have no I/E, conflicts or unresolved addresses. An active lease's unresolved is its planned low targets minus clean I and E; it therefore contains all low targets while quarantined. Canary addresses never appear as planned lows. Report conflicts even when alias has higher priority." ✓

"### Causal application census and device exchanges
A live application row is eligible only when its lease is usable, its target is in clean I or E, and the earliest witness for that role is <=its event time. All other live app rows contribute once to unbound_applications, including in inactive/quarantined leases. For each eligible (lease,target,service), only maximum attempt rows decide status. All such rows must agree on the same parsed open signature to yield open; all must be closed to yield closed; any other combination yields unknown. Identical signatures across distinct row identities agree; different signatures disagree. Missing rows and timeouts are unknown. Malformed open wire data is unknown and contributes one protocol_errors per eligible latest-attempt row identity, even if another row disagrees. Earlier attempts and unbound rows contribute no protocol errors." ✓

"TCP open signature is the constant tcp. An ADB open payload is exactly one packet: ... Reject trailing bytes." ✓

"A sync open payload is exactly two consecutive frames ... Parsing/recursion errors are bad wire data; dictionary order and serialization are irrelevant. plistlib's parsed dictionary semantics apply to duplicate keys." ✓

"For every lease/service report clean-role subsets internal_open, internal_closed, external_open, external_closed. Unknowns are the remaining role addresses. internal_only equals internal_open exactly when E is nonempty and every E address is closed for that service; otherwise it is empty. This is an evidence comparison, not a physical attribution claim." ✓

"### Follow-up obligations, quotas and certificate
There are at most 4096 requests {id,at,lease,target,service,group}. at is a query time; lease/service references exist; group names a request-quota node. A request is active iff its target is in that query's clean I and that service is unknown there. Its activity is frozen at its own query: later snapshots do not cancel the obligation. Inactive requests cannot be assigned. Distinct request IDs are distinct obligations even if their other fields coincide." ✓

"There are at most 8192 offers {id,time,service,prefix,capacity,cost,group,requests}. Service/group references exist. Capacity is 0–4096 and cost is 0–10^9. requests is a list of distinct known request IDs; total listed pairs across offers is at most 262144. An assignment is allowed iff the request is active and listed, services agree, request.at<=offer.time<request.lease.end, and its target is in the offer prefix. Offers have no other implicit capacity sharing." ✓

"Each quota list contains0–4096 nodes {id,parent,capacity}. Parent is null or a known node in that same list; no cycles; the node-to-root path contains at most 32 nodes. Capacity is 0–4096. The lists can be forests with multiple roots. Each assigned request consumes one unit at its group and every ancestor in the request forest. Each assignment also consumes one unit at its offer's group and every ancestor in the offer forest. Each request occurs at most once and each offer's assignment count is at most its capacity. Capacity zero is meaningful." ✓

"Maximize the number assigned; among all maximum-cardinality plans minimize the integer sum of offer costs, one cost per assignment. Any plan attaining both objectives is accepted; there is no further tie break. Empty optimum is valid. Assignments are sorted by request ID. Each is {request,offer,send,finish} with base64 packet arrays certifying the outbound probe for that request's service" ✓

"TCP: both arrays empty.
ADB: send is one CNXN packet, arg0=0x01000000, arg1=4096, body exactly UTF-8 host::zgrab2; finish is one CLSE0x45534c43 packet with both arguments zero and empty body. Both use the length/checksum/magic encoding above.
Sync: send is two length-prefixed plist frames in ProductVersion/ProductName order. Each parsed dictionary is exactly {Key,Label,ProtocolVersion,Request}, with that Key, Label=usbmuxd, ProtocolVersion=2, Request=GetValue, all strings. Equivalent XML/binary serializations are accepted. Frame lengths are computed from actual body bytes,1–65532. Finish is empty." ✓

"No packet is transmitted. Certificates are validated semantically; matching the starter's particular plist bytes is not required. There are no source-style, module-layout or auxiliary-file scoring requirements." ✓

"## Result structure and order
A normal result has exactly manifest,rejected,snapshots,active_requests,plan. Manifest and rejection order are defined above. Snapshots are in increasing query order and each is {at,ledger,unbound_applications,leases}. leases contains every lease, ordered lexically by ID, each with keys lease,state,conflicts,internal,external,unresolved,services. Each services array contains every service lexically by ID, each with keys id,internal_open,internal_closed,external_open,external_closed,internal_only,protocol_errors. All address arrays are distinct and numerically increasing. All counts are exact integers. active_requests contains {id,active} for every request, lexically by ID; active is a JSON boolean. plan is {resolved,cost,assignments}, where resolved is assignment count and cost is its exact integer sum." ✓
